content_units: Balanced Retirement Mix for a 29-Year-Old
For a   29-year-old with moderate risk tolerance and a 25+ year horizon  ,   Portfolio 1 (70/20/10)   is the most balanced choice of the three.
Why it stands out:
- It keeps a strong   growth engine   through stocks.
- It has meaningful   international diversification  .
- It includes a modest   bond cushion   to reduce volatility without dragging long-term growth too much.
Allocation Comparison Table
Portfolio   Allocation (A/B/C)   Stock/Bond Mix   Risk Level   Diversification   Best Fit
Portfolio 1   70/20/10   90/10   Moderate   Strong   Long horizon, moderate risk, wants growth with some stability
Portfolio 2   55/25/20   80/20   Moderately conservative   Strongest overall   Investor who wants smoother ride and less drawdown stress
Portfolio 3   80/15/5   95/5   Moderately aggressive   Good   Investor comfortable with bigger swings for higher growth potential
Risk and Diversification Breakdown
Portfolio 1: 70/20/10
-   Fund A 70%  : broad US stock market core
-   Fund B 20%  : international stock exposure
-   Fund C 10%  : bonds for stability
Why it feels balanced:
- Roughly   90% stocks / 10% bonds   is still growth-focused, which fits a long retirement timeline.
- The   20% international slice   helps reduce overreliance on the US market.
- The   10% bond allocation   can soften downturns and make rebalancing easier during market drops.
Trade-offs:
- Still likely to fall significantly in a bad bear market.
- Less upside than the most aggressive option, but meaningfully steadier.
Best for:
- A younger investor who wants to invest for decades but does   not   want an all-stock portfolio.
- Someone who can handle volatility, but prefers a little shock absorption.
Portfolio 2: 55/25/20
-   Fund A 55%
-   Fund B 25%
-   Fund C 20%
Why it is lower risk:
- The   20% bond position   makes returns smoother and usually reduces portfolio drawdowns.
- The   25% international weight   gives broad global stock diversification.
Trade-offs:
- Better downside control, but likely lower long-run growth than Portfolio 1 or 3.
- For a 29-year-old, this may be a little conservative unless volatility really affects behavior.
Best for:
- Someone with   moderate-to-lower risk tolerance  .
- An investor who values staying calm during downturns and wants a portfolio that is easier to stick with.
Portfolio 3: 80/15/5
-   Fund A 80%
-   Fund B 15%
-   Fund C 5%
Why it is the most aggressive:
- At about   95% stocks / 5% bonds  , this portfolio is built for maximum long-term growth.
- It will generally be more volatile and can see larger short-term losses.
Trade-offs:
- Least protection in market declines.
- Lower international exposure than the other two, so diversification is a bit weaker.
- Great on paper for long horizons, but only if the investor can truly tolerate sharp drawdowns.
Best for:
- Someone with   moderate-to-high risk tolerance  .
- An investor who will not panic during a major market decline and wants to maximize growth.
Best Choice for Moderate Risk
Recommended: Portfolio 1
It best matches the stated priorities in order:
-   25+ year horizon   supports a high stock allocation.
-   Moderate risk tolerance   argues against going too aggressive.
-   Diversification   is solid with both US and international stocks plus a stabilizing bond sleeve.
A practical way to think about it:
-   Portfolio 3   is best if growth is the priority and volatility won’t change behavior.
-   Portfolio 2   is best if emotional comfort and smoother returns matter more.
-   Portfolio 1   sits in the middle and is the strongest all-around fit.
Portfolio Fit by Investor Type
Option 1:   Portfolio 1 — Best overall balance     Strong growth potential with some downside cushion   Best fit for moderate risk over 25+ years
Option 2:   Portfolio 2 — Smoother ride     More bonds and global diversification reduce volatility   Best for conservative-leaning moderate investors
Option 3:   Portfolio 3 — Growth-first     Highest expected long-run growth, but biggest swings   Best for aggressive investors with strong discipline
